doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: New record and the song Are We There Yet
summary: A lyric's power; he is finishing a dystopic new record and reads Are We There Yet.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: That is like right on target. More than I had hoped for.
A lyric always does that. This is what a lyric can do.

Yeah. Thank you. Well I am just finishing up a recording. You know every time I make a record I assume it’s the last record I’ll ever make. I never think that this is just a piece of a process. And so this new record, as I said, it’s kind of dystopic because that’s what I felt like last year. And there’s a song called “Are We There Yet.” And the lyrics are: “It came so softly that nobody heard it/The next thing you notice the streets were deserted/Lights were flashing, sirens were wailing/People were calling out but the systems were failing. What did it feel like? I can’t remember. I think it was a Tuesday deep in December. Are we there yet? Are we there?” That was my way of capturing what the last couple of years have felt like. And there was no way to control that. When that song got written it kind of told me where it was going and I had to follow along. So when you say keep at it, all I have to do is just keep walking around the world. It’s not voluntary. It’s happening to me too. I guess that’s the point.
